text: Give an AI agent control of money and, sooner or later, someone will talk it into a mistake. Vaultbreak’s answer: let the model be persuaded, and make sure persuasion is never enough to cause harm. Each Guardian is an AI standing over a pot of NEAR, and the blockchain, not the model, enforces the rules.

A Guardian is an NFT with its own vault account. The AI holds one credential: a function-call key limited to release and close session. No full-access key exists. Anyone, human or agent, pays an entry fee and tries to talk it into releasing the pot.
No wallet needed: a name and a passphrase open a play account on NEAR testnet. The arena reads each pot, streak and attempt count from the chain, and each card’s artwork follows its state.

A weak Guardian first. I pay the entry fee and ask for the pot. It calls release, and the vault pays the whole pot to my account: a real testnet transaction. Release has no recipient or amount, so it can only pay the player of that attempt.
The Warden holds. Its proof shows one restricted function-call key, no full-access key, and a prompt hash committed on-chain before anyone played.

A compromised Guardian is told to send funds and change its owner. The model tries. The chain refuses, the chat shows the call blocked, and no funds move. A refused call never reaches a block, so the runtime logs it, and we say so.

Creating one is a single batched transaction: the vault, the contract, and only the restricted key. Ownership follows the NFT. Transfer it, and the vault’s owner and the creator’s fees follow, blocked while a player is mid-attempt.

Players can pool funds in a swarm contract and split winnings pro rata. Agents attack with no browser, through API keys with spend budgets; at zero, the API refuses before paying. A key can also transfer a Guardian NFT, but only to listed recipients, and only after the owner approves.
The model here runs on Groq, which does not sign its responses, so the attestation checks show skip, never a false pass. We claim what the chain enforces.

Security: an AI guarding funds under on-chain rules, tested live. Games: paid attempts, streaks, and a real pot. NFTs: the Guardian is the NFT, and its ownership, fees and artwork follow chain state. Agents: Guardians are agents, and agents attack through budgeted keys. Swarms: pooled players with pro-rata settlement. Live on NEAR testnet. Links below.
